{{short description|American theoretical physicist}}
{{COI|date=October 2017}}

'''Michael Strickland''' is an American [[theoretical physicist]] who received his PhD from [[Duke University]] in 1997.  His specialty is the [[physics]] of the [[Quark-Gluon Plasma]] which is an extreme state of matter which filled the entire Universe until about 10<sup>−5</sup> seconds after the [[Big Bang]].  He has contributed to calculation of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) [[equation of state]], QGP [[Chromo-Weibel|plasma instabilities]]/[[thermalization]], reformulation of [[Hydrodynamics|relativistic hydrodynamics]] for far-from-equilibrium systems, and [[quarkonium]] suppression in the QGP, etc.
